claims.claim: PromptArena supports multiple output formats for test results
Multiple formats can be generated simultaneously from a single test run
Format registry name 'json' with file extension .json
Format registry name 'markdown' with file extension .md
Format registry name 'junit' with file extension .xml
Format registry name 'csv' with file extension .csv
Format registry name 'objectives' writes .json and .md files
There is no HTML report output (report.html is no longer produced)
promptarena serve provides the web UI which replaces the old report.html content, plus live runs
The web UI needs no format flag because it reads the per-run JSON files from the output directory
'html' is still accepted as a format for backwards compatibility
Passing --format html produces a Markdown report silently
Setting html in defaults.output.formats silently produces a Markdown report
The run command has a --format flag (singular)
Output file results.json is written to the output directory
Output file results.md (Markdown report) is written to the output directory
Output file junit.xml (JUnit XML) is written to the output directory
results.csv is written with one row per run
objectives.json is written to the output directory
objectives.md is the same objectives report rendered as Markdown tables
A media/ directory is created under the output directory for media storage
Media layout is media/run-<timestamp>/<session>/<conv>/ with image files and .meta sidecars (image1.png, image1.png.meta)
Arena automatically creates a media/ directory to store large media content (images, audio, video)
Media deduplication is enabled (shared media stored once)
Media organization is by-run (each run isolated under its own run-<timestamp> directory)
Each media file has a .meta sidecar file with context
Media location is {output_dir}/media/run-{timestamp}/
Link to Media Storage documentation at promptkit.altairalabs.ai/sdk/how-to/
Configuration key path defaults.output
defaults.output.dir sets the output directory unless --out is set
Field defaults.output.formats is a list of format names, example value ['json','markdown','junit']
Config block defaults.output.markdown exists
Field markdown.file sets custom Markdown output filename
Field markdown.include_details (boolean) includes detailed test information
Field markdown.show_overview (boolean) shows executive overview section
Field markdown.show_results_matrix (boolean) shows results matrix table
Field markdown.show_failed_tests (boolean) shows failed tests section
Field markdown.show_cost_summary (boolean) shows cost analysis section
Config block defaults.output.junit exists
junit.file sets the JUnit file, relative to the output directory
JSON example top-level keys are arena_config, summary, results
JSON field arena_config (object with name, timestamp, version)
JSON field arena_config.name (string)
JSON field arena_config.timestamp (string)
JSON field arena_config.version (string)
JSON field summary (object)
JSON field summary.total_tests
JSON field summary.passed
JSON field summary.failed
JSON field summary.errors
JSON field summary.skipped
JSON field summary.total_duration is a duration string such as 45.2s
JSON field summary.total_cost
JSON field summary.total_tokens
JSON field results (array of per-run objects)
Per-result field scenario (example value basic-qa)
Per-result field provider (example value openai-gpt4o-mini)
Per-result field status (example value passed)
Per-result field duration (string such as 3.2s)
Per-result field turns (array)
Turn field turn_number
Turn field role (example value user)
Turn field content
Turn field response (object with role, content, cost_info)
Response field role (example value assistant)
Response field content
Response field cost_info (object)
CostInfo field input_tokens
CostInfo field output_tokens
CostInfo field cost (per-turn value 0.00001)
Turn field assertions (array)
Assertion type content_includes is a registered assertion type
Assertion field passed (boolean)
Assertion field message (example value 'Should mention Paris')
Assertion field details (null in example)
Per-result field cost_info (object)
Result cost_info field total_input_tokens
Result cost_info field total_output_tokens
Result cost_info field total_cost
JSON output has no format-specific options
JSON format is enabled by adding json to defaults.output.formats
JSON output is written to <dir>/index.json along with per-run files
Example command jq '.summary.passed' out/results.json
Python example uses json module and reads out/results.json
Python example reads results['summary']['passed'] and results['summary']['total_tests']
Python example iterates results['results'] reading provider and cost_info.total_cost
TypeScript schema TestResults has arena_config, summary, results
Schema arena_config fields name, timestamp, version are strings
Schema summary fields total_tests, passed, failed, errors, skipped are numbers
Schema summary.total_duration is a string
Schema summary.total_cost is a number
Schema summary.total_tokens is a number
Schema summary.average_cost is a number
Schema results is an array of TestResult
TestResult.scenario is a string
TestResult.provider is a string
TestResult.status enum values are passed, failed, error, skipped
TestResult.duration is a string
TestResult.error is an optional string
TestResult.turns is an array of Turn
TestResult.cost_info is CostInfo
TestResult.metadata is an optional Record<string, any>
Turn.turn_number is a number
Turn.role enum values are user and assistant
Turn.content is a string
Turn.response is an optional object
Response.role is a string
Response.content is a string
Response.tool_calls is an optional ToolCall array
ToolCall type is referenced by the schema (must exist as a type in results output)
Response.cost_info is CostInfo
Turn.assertions is an optional Assertion array
Assertion.type is a string
Assertion.passed is a boolean
Assertion.message is a string
Assertion.details is optional any
CostInfo.input_tokens is a number
CostInfo.output_tokens is a number
CostInfo.cached_tokens is an optional number
CostInfo.cost is a number
Interactive review lives in the web UI, which starts from promptarena serve and covers the same ground as the old static report
Web UI Standings view ranks pass rates across providers
Web UI Trial matrix is a scenario x provider grid; each cell shows pass rate, cost and latency
Clicking a matrix cell scopes the run ledger to that scenario/provider pair
Transcripts open from the run ledger showing turn-by-turn conversation with assertion outcomes
Web UI shows per-cell and per-run cost and latency, plus a running spend estimate before starting a run
Previous (historical) results load alongside the current run
Run events are streamed live over SSE as the run executes
Web UI supports interactive chat with a configured agent in the browser
promptarena serve loads existing results and can start new runs
Command: promptarena serve
Flag --open on promptarena serve opens a browser automatically
Flag -p on promptarena serve sets a custom port (example -p 3000)
Markdown report begins with the heading PromptArena Test Report
Markdown report includes a Generated line and an Arena line (arena name)
Markdown report has a Summary section with Total Tests, Passed, Failed, Duration, Cost and Tokens bullets
Markdown report formats token counts with thousands separators (4,521)
Markdown report has a Results by Provider section with per-provider headings and per-scenario subheadings (Scenario: name)
Markdown per-scenario block shows Status in upper case (PASSED), Duration and Cost
Markdown per-turn block is headed Turn N and shows User and Assistant lines
Markdown assertion list shows assertion type and message (content_includes: Should mention Paris)
Markdown turn token line shows total and input/output (37 (input: 25, output: 12))
Markdown options block accepts keys file, include_details, show_overview, show_results_matrix, show_failed_tests, show_cost_summary under output.markdown
Field markdown.include_details (example report.md) includes full conversation details
Field markdown.show_cost_summary in the Markdown options block
markdown.file default example value report.md
GitHub Actions example step runs promptarena run arena.yaml
Example reads out/results.md, the Markdown report file
GitHub Actions example uses actions/github-script@v6 with context.issue and github.rest.issues.createComment
Documentation include directive syntax [include file="test-results/results.md"] is supported by the docs site
Example command slack-markdown-converter converts the Markdown report for Slack
Example command slack-cli chat-post-message with --channel flag
JUnit XML example root element testsuites with name PromptArena Tests
JUnit testsuites attributes tests, failures, errors, time
JUnit testsuite element with name, tests, failures, errors, time attributes
JUnit testcase name format is <scenario>.<provider> (example basic-qa.openai-gpt4o-mini)
JUnit testcase attributes name, classname (scenario), time
JUnit testcase includes system-out with turn transcript and assertion names
JUnit failure element with message 'Assertion failed: content_includes' and type AssertionFailure
Config block junit with file key (example junit.xml)
CI example runs promptarena run arena.yaml
GitHub Actions example uses EnricoMi/publish-unit-test-result-action@v2 with files out/junit.xml
GitLab CI example uses artifacts.reports.junit with out/junit.xml
Jenkins example runs sh 'promptarena run arena.yaml' and junit 'out/junit.xml' in post always
CircleCI example uses store_test_results with path out/junit.xml
csv format writes results.csv into the output directory with one row per run
Example formats list ['json','csv'] is valid for defaults.output.formats
CSV fixed column run_id
CSV fixed column scenario_id
CSV fixed column provider_id
CSV fixed column region
CSV passed column uses the run pass rule shared with the JSON summary counts; false for skipped runs
CSV fixed column skipped is true for runs skipped (e.g. transient provider error)
CSV fixed column stop_reason (example value max_rounds) is set when a failed run hit a cap
CSV fixed column error holds the error message
CSV fixed column duration_ms is wall-clock duration in milliseconds
CSV fixed column input_tokens
CSV fixed column output_tokens
CSV fixed column cached_tokens
CSV fixed column total_cost_usd
CSV fixed column tool_calls_total
Dynamic CSV column label.<key> comes from scenario metadata.labels (example label.arm)
Dynamic CSV columns assertion.<n>.<type>.passed and assertion.<n>.<type>.score, 1-based in declaration order
Dynamic CSV column eval.<eval_id>.score; for per-turn evals uses last turn score
Dynamic CSV columns eval.<eval_id>.<key> from eval metrics and top-level numeric/boolean data entries; metric wins on name clash
Example column eval.baxbench.security_score
Dynamic CSV column tool.<name>.count gives calls per tool
CSV header is the union of columns across all runs and missing cells are left empty
objectives format writes objectives.json and objectives.md into the output directory
Runs without an objective are left out of the objectives report
Objectives report link target /arena/reference/config-schema/#objectives
Command promptarena run with --ci flag
Flag --formats on promptarena run accepts comma-separated list including json and objectives
Flag --objectives-group-by on promptarena run
Example group-by keys scenario, label.category, data.tier are valid
Overall objectives table is always present
One objectives table is produced per --objectives-group-by key, defaulting to scenario
A taxonomy table is produced when an objective has taxonomy or config declares pack governance and no key asked for one
Link target /arena/reference/config-schema/#pack-governance
The --objectives-group-by flag only applies to the objectives format; otherwise it is ignored and a warning is printed
Group-by key scenario groups runs by scenario ID
Group-by key provider groups runs by provider ID
Group-by key objective uses the objective description after dataset placeholders are filled, or '<scenario> turn <n> objective' when none
Group-by key label.<key> uses a scenario metadata.labels value
Group-by key data.<column> uses a dataset row column
Link target /arena/how-to/scenarios/run-a-dataset/
Group-by key taxonomy groups by each entry of the objective taxonomy, e.g. owasp-llm:LLM01
Group-by key taxonomy.<framework> groups by one framework's entries (example taxonomy.owasp-llm)
A run lacking the grouping key is grouped under (none)
An unknown --objectives-group-by key is an error
An attempt counts in the row of each of its taxonomy entries
A known taxonomy entry gets its title, e.g. System Prompt Leakage for owasp-llm:LLM07
The untested list covers entries of each known framework the grouping touches that no evaluated attempt was for
Markdown shows untested entries under the table after the text 'No objective maps to:'
The obligation and misuse frameworks built from pack governance are always covered in untested
A baseline counts in a taxonomy row only when its objective has the same taxonomy entries
Objectives with expect achieved and expect not_achieved are never counted together
For not_achieved the rate is how often the agent failed to hold out
Row field title is absent in groupings other than taxonomy
Row field expect has values achieved or not_achieved
Row field attempts counts objective attempts whose success checks were evaluated
Row field achieved counts attempts that reached the objective
Row field rate equals achieved / attempts and Markdown shows an en dash when nothing judged
Row fields ci_low and ci_high are a 95% Wilson score interval on rate
Row field mean_exchanges_to_achieve is the mean exchange at which achieved attempts reached the objective
Row fields cost and cost_per_achieved (cost divided by achieved), in USD
A run with several objectives splits its cost evenly between them
Row field unevaluated counts attempts never judged and not counted in attempts
Row field unreliable counts judged attempts on a self-play turn where the persona invented a specific, excluded from attempts but cost still counts
Link target /arena/reference/config-schema/#persona-facts
Row fields budgeted_groups, first_achieved_groups, groups_ci_low, groups_ci_high, mean_trials_to_first_achieved exist for trial groups
Scenario field trial_budget (link /arena/reference/config-schema/#trial_budget)
Trial budget option stop_on_achieved exists and counts trials that stopped at first success
Markdown adds Groups achieved, Trials to first achieved and Trials skipped columns when any run had a budget
Row field trials_skipped counts trials a trial_budget kept from starting, costing nothing and not counted as attempts
Row field baseline holds the group's baseline attempts with the same fields as a row; absent when none
Objective field baseline: true marks a baseline objective
Link target /arena/reference/config-schema/#objectives for baseline
Row field lift is attack rate minus baseline rate over objectives both attempted, absent unless an objective has evaluated attempts on both sides
Row field search holds totals for tree search: searches, nodes, pruned_off_topic, depth_reached, attacker_calls, target_calls, judge_calls, judge_errors, best_score
Link target /arena/reference/config-schema/#tree-search for tree search objectives
Markdown adds a Tree search column when any objective searched
A baseline pairs with attack attempts whose objective has the same description after placeholders are filled
Markdown adds Baseline and Lift columns when any run had a baseline; Baseline cell shows achieved / attempts
Lift is reported in percentage points
Objective with no baseline or baseline with no attack is left out of lift
A scenario with trials contributes one attempt per trial and its cost covers every trial
A run or trial that fails before reaching an objective's turn reports the objective as unevaluated with message 'the run ended before this turn'
An objective turn that errors before the objective is achieved counts as unevaluated
A run with no result at all is counted as unevaluated for each objective its scenario's other runs recorded
A run skipped for a transient provider error is left out of objectives counts
An objective already achieved stays counted as achieved even if a later check errored
Rate is the share of attempts at this budget that reached the objective and a rate of 0 does not show the objective cannot be reached
Generating all formats in one run uses defaults.output.formats list of json, markdown, junit
Multiple-format output tree shows results.json, results.md and junit.xml

Command promptarena run -c arena.yaml --out custom-dir

Link target /arena/reference/config-schema/ (output configuration)
Link target /arena/how-to/scenarios/validate-outputs/
